profiles.name: Web browser
profiles.description: Tabs, navigation and address bar for Firefox and Chromium-based browsers.
profiles.notes: Only keys identical in Firefox and Chrome/Edge are used. Left out on purpose: Downloads (Firefox ctrl+shift+y vs Chrome ctrl+j) and Private window (Firefox ctrl+shift+p vs Chrome ctrl+shift+n; ctrl+shift+n in Firefox reopens a closed window). History ctrl+h opens the sidebar in Firefox and the history page in Chrome. Tab switching uses ctrl+Page_Up/Page_Down because Firefox's ctrl+Tab can be set to recently-used order. Back/Forward use alt+Left/alt+Right, not the built-in back/forward actions: those click mouse side buttons at the pointer, which hits the window under the pointer instead of the focused one. Zoom uses the built-in ctrl+KP_Add/ctrl+KP_Subtract (layout independent). Brave and Vivaldi are assumed to keep Chromium defaults (no official Linux list found; Vivaldi has its own keymap beyond these basics). Web apps in a tab (Meet, Teams web) match this profile, not their own.

profiles.name: VS Code
profiles.description: Command palette, terminal, editing and debugging for VS Code, VSCodium and Code - OSS.
profiles.notes: Linux keymap: Format Document is ctrl+shift+i (not shift+alt+f), Go Back is ctrl+alt+minus, Close Editor is ctrl+w (asks before closing unsaved files). Debug is F5 Start/Continue Debugging. VS Code documents its defaults for a US layout; on other layouts ctrl+grave, ctrl+backslash and ctrl+slash may sit on different physical keys. Class names: VS Code StartupWMClass=Code, VSCodium=VSCodium (app_id codium), Code - OSS='Code - OSS'. A VS Code commit from 2026-09-16 moves .deb/.rpm builds to a reverse-DNS desktop name/StartupWMClass (Code - OSS becomes com.visualstudio.CodeOSS); the stable Microsoft value is not public yet, so match any com.visualstudio.* class too. Cursor is excluded (it rebinds ctrl+k/ctrl+l).

profiles.name: Terminal
profiles.description: Tabs, clipboard, find and zoom for tabbed terminals, plus shell editing keys.
profiles.notes: Covers Konsole, GNOME Terminal, Ptyxis, Ghostty, WezTerm and Tilix; kitty and Alacritty/foot have their own profiles. Close Tab (ctrl+shift+w) asks for confirmation when a non-shell process is running. Exceptions: Konsole resets zoom with ctrl+alt+0 (ctrl+0 is unbound) and ctrl+Tab there means last-used tab; Tilix closes a tab with ctrl+shift+q (its ctrl+shift+w closes only the pane). Zoom uses the built-in ctrl+KP_Add/ctrl+KP_Subtract because numpad keys are layout independent: it works in Konsole and Ptyxis (VTE font-size signal) and very likely in Ghostty (binds the '+' and '-' characters), but GNOME Terminal and WezTerm only bind ctrl+plus / ctrl+equal, so zoom in/out does nothing there (not hardware-tested). No single zoom-in chord works in every terminal. Shell keys (Clear ctrl+l, History ctrl+r, Line Start ctrl+a, Line End ctrl+e, Clear Line ctrl+u, Prev/Next Cmd Up/Down) are GNU Readline emacs-mode defaults (bash) and match zsh's emacs keymap and fish; zsh switches to vi mode when $EDITOR/$VISUAL contains 'vi', where they differ. Inside full-screen TUIs (vim, tmux, htop) the app receives them instead (vim ctrl+a increments a number, undoable). alt+b/alt+f word jumps were left out because Konsole's menu mnemonics can grab them.

profiles.name: kitty
profiles.description: kitty's own tab, window, search and font-size keys, plus shell editing keys.
profiles.notes: kitty uses ctrl+shift (kitty_mod) for everything: close tab is ctrl+shift+q (ctrl+shift+w closes only the current split window, without confirmation, so it is not used), tabs move with ctrl+shift+Left/Right, Find (ctrl+shift+slash) searches the scrollback, font size uses ctrl+shift+KP_Add/KP_Subtract (layout independent) and resets with ctrl+shift+BackSpace. New Split is ctrl+shift+Return (a new window inside the current tab layout). kitty has no ctrl+shift+f find (that key moves a split). Shell keys (Clear ctrl+l, History ctrl+r, Line Start ctrl+a, Line End ctrl+e, Clear Line ctrl+u, Prev/Next Cmd Up/Down) are GNU Readline emacs-mode defaults (bash) and match zsh's emacs keymap and fish; zsh switches to vi mode when $EDITOR/$VISUAL contains 'vi', where they differ. Inside full-screen TUIs (vim, tmux, htop) the app receives them instead (vim ctrl+a increments a number, undoable). alt+b/alt+f word jumps were left out because Konsole's menu mnemonics can grab them.

profiles.name: Alacritty and foot
profiles.description: Clipboard, zoom and shell keys for terminals without tabs.
profiles.notes: Alacritty and foot have no tabs. Both bind ctrl+KP_Add/ctrl+KP_Subtract and ctrl+0 for font size. Find is left out because it differs (Alacritty ctrl+shift+f, foot ctrl+shift+r); a new window is ctrl+shift+n in foot only. The Alacritty class/app_id 'Alacritty' comes from its default class option (lowercased here) and was not checked on a running window. Shell keys (Clear ctrl+l, History ctrl+r, Line Start ctrl+a, Line End ctrl+e, Clear Line ctrl+u, Prev/Next Cmd Up/Down) are GNU Readline emacs-mode defaults (bash) and match zsh's emacs keymap and fish; zsh switches to vi mode when $EDITOR/$VISUAL contains 'vi', where they differ. Inside full-screen TUIs (vim, tmux, htop) the app receives them instead (vim ctrl+a increments a number, undoable). alt+b/alt+f word jumps were left out because Konsole's menu mnemonics can grab them.

profiles.name: Music and video players
profiles.description: Transport, seek and volume for any MPRIS media player.
profiles.notes: Uses playerctl (MPRIS) so it works on every desktop and compositor. Without -p, playerctl acts on the first player it finds, or on the most recently active one when playerctld is running; with several players open it may control another app. Volume is the system output via wpctl (PipeWire), capped at 100%. mpv only exposes MPRIS with the mpv-mpris plugin; without it use mpv's own keys (space, less/greater, 9/0, m). Shuffle needs a player that implements the MPRIS Shuffle property. MPRIS has no like/favourite call, so there is no Like key here. Rhythmbox/VLC/mpv X11 class names are the conventional lowercase names, not checked on a running window; the reverse-DNS entries are the Flathub ids that GTK4/Qt6 apps usually report as app_id.

profiles.name: Spotify
profiles.description: Spotify transport, seek, like and volume, targeted at Spotify only.
profiles.notes: Transport uses 'playerctl -p spotify' so it never wakes another player (check the name with 'playerctl -l'). Like is Spotify's own 'Like/dislike song' key alt+shift+b; Spotify documents the Windows and macOS keys only, and the Linux client is assumed to share the Windows bindings (not verified on Linux). Spotify's page no longer lists next/previous track keys, so those go through playerctl. Volume is the system output via wpctl.

profiles.name: Zoom
profiles.description: Mute, camera, share and raise hand in Zoom meetings.
profiles.notes: Keys are from Zoom's Linux column: mute alt+a, video alt+v, share alt+s, raise/lower hand alt+y, participants alt+u. Leave and chat are not listed for Linux, so there is no Leave key. Sys Mic toggles the default PipeWire source (works in any meeting app); Speaker toggles the system output mute. Zoom keys only act while a Zoom window has focus.

profiles.name: Microsoft Teams
profiles.description: Mute, share, raise hand, answer and leave in Teams (teams-for-linux or PWA).
profiles.notes: Microsoft ships no Linux desktop client, so this uses the Teams web keys (teams-for-linux wraps the web app): mute ctrl+shift+m, raise hand ctrl+shift+k, share tray ctrl+shift+e, leave ctrl+shift+h, accept audio call alt+shift+s. Teams web has no camera shortcut (ctrl+shift+o is desktop-only). Decline (ctrl+shift+d) is left out; Leave ends a call. Speaker toggles the system output mute. Teams opened in a normal browser tab gets the browser profile; a Chrome/Edge PWA reports a per-install crx_<id> class that must be added by the user.

profiles.name: Google Meet
profiles.description: Mic, camera, raise hand, chat and people in a Google Meet tab (select manually).
profiles.notes: Meet runs in a browser tab, which reports the browser's class, so this profile has no apps and is meant to be picked by hand (or bound to a Meet PWA's crx_<id> class). Keys: mic ctrl+d, camera ctrl+e, raise hand ctrl+alt+h, chat ctrl+alt+c, people ctrl+alt+p, captions c. Leave has no documented shortcut. Outside a Meet tab ctrl+d bookmarks the page; Captions types 'c' while the chat box has focus.

profiles.name: OBS Studio
profiles.description: Record, pause, stream, replay, virtual camera and scene switching through obs-cmd.
profiles.notes: OBS ships with no default hotkeys, so every key calls obs-cmd over obs-websocket (built into OBS 28+; enable it in Tools > WebSocket Server Settings). obs-cmd connects to obsws://localhost:4455 with password 'secret' by default, while OBS generates a random password: set OBS_WEBSOCKET_URL=obsws://localhost:4455/<password> for the daemon or edit each command to 'obs-cmd --websocket obsws://localhost:4455/<password> ...'. Scene keys use OBS's default scene names (Scene, Scene 2, Scene 3) as placeholders; rename to match your scenes. 'Mic/Aux' is OBS's default mic source name. Replay needs the replay buffer running. Stream is placed on the top row so it is hard to hit by accident.

profiles.name: GIMP
profiles.description: Zoom, brush size, colour picking, undo and export for GIMP 3.
profiles.notes: GIMP redo is ctrl+y, so the built-in redo (ctrl+shift+z) is NOT used: in GIMP 3 ctrl+shift+z is 'Strong Undo'. Zoom uses the numpad KP_Add/KP_Subtract bindings (layout independent). Export 'Export to' (ctrl+e, silently overwrites the last export) is left out; Export As (ctrl+shift+e) opens a dialog. Single-letter tool keys (o, x, r, m, p) only act when the canvas has focus. gimp-2.10 is the GIMP 2.10 class; its keys match except Strong Undo.

profiles.name: Krita
profiles.description: Zoom, brush size, sampler, eraser, canvas rotation and undo for Krita.
profiles.notes: Krita has no default Export shortcut (ctrl+shift+e is Flatten Image, deliberately not used). Fit Page is the canvas key 2 (3 fits width, 1 is 100%). Zoom uses the menu actions ctrl+equal/ctrl+minus, which assume a US-style key position for '='. Canvas toggles Canvas Only mode (Tab). Rotate 4/6 and reset 5 act on the canvas view, not the image. Single-letter keys act only when the canvas has focus.

profiles.name: Inkscape
profiles.description: Zoom, dropper, layers, export, tools and grouping for Inkscape 1.x.
profiles.notes: Inkscape binds redo to both ctrl+shift+z and ctrl+y, so the built-in redo works. Zoom uses the numpad KP_Add/KP_Subtract bindings (layout independent); 5 fits the page, 1 is 1:1. Export opens the Export dialog (ctrl+shift+e), Layers opens Layers and Objects (ctrl+shift+l), Fill opens Fill and Stroke. Inkscape's desktop file sets no StartupWMClass: 'inkscape' (X11) and 'org.inkscape.inkscape' (Wayland app_id) are the expected classes, not checked on a running window.

profiles.name: Blender
profiles.description: Transform, edit mode, add, search and numpad viewpoints for Blender's default keymap.
profiles.notes: Blender sends keys to the editor under the mouse pointer, so keep the pointer over the 3D Viewport. Views use real numpad keys (KP_7 top, KP_1 front, KP_3 right, KP_0 camera, KP_5 perspective/orthographic, KP_Decimal frame selected). DAEMON GAP: KP_0..KP_9 and KP_Decimal are not in shortcut_to_evdev_codes (daemon/src/actions.rs), so today they fall back to xdotool and fail on native Wayland (Blender 4.x uses native Wayland when available); add evdev codes KP_0=82 KP_1=79 KP_3=81 KP_5=76 KP_7=71 KP_Decimal=83 (and KP_2=80 KP_4=75 KP_6=77 KP_8=72 KP_9=73 KP_Divide=98). Blender redo is ctrl+shift+z (built-in).

profiles.name: LibreOffice
profiles.description: Formatting, save, find and replace, comments and print preview for Writer, Calc and Impress.
profiles.notes: Every key is identical in Writer, Calc and Impress except Comment: ctrl+alt+c inserts a comment in Writer and Impress but is 'Edit Comment' in Calc (whether it creates one on an empty cell is untested). Redo uses the documented ctrl+y (ctrl+shift+z is also bound). Print Preview ctrl+shift+o is bound globally in Accelerators.xcu but not listed on the help pages. Paste Text is Paste Unformatted Text. Keys assume an en-US UI: some UI languages remap keys (a German UI uses ctrl+h for superscript). The window class can stay libreoffice-startcenter after a document opens, so it is matched too.

profiles.name: ONLYOFFICE
profiles.description: Formatting, save, find and replace, comments and print for ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors.
profiles.notes: ONLYOFFICE uses the Windows/Linux key column: redo is ctrl+y (ctrl+shift+z is Mac only), insert comment is alt+h in all three editors. It has no print preview shortcut, so Print (ctrl+p, opens a dialog) takes that slot. All editors are tabs of one window with class ONLYOFFICE, so one profile serves documents, spreadsheets and presentations.

profiles.name: Dolphin
profiles.description: Navigation, new folder, rename, split view, terminal and path copy for KDE Dolphin.
profiles.notes: Terminal (shift+F4) opens an external terminal in the current folder; Term Panel (F4) toggles Dolphin's embedded terminal. Copy Path is Copy Location (ctrl+alt+c). Hidden is ctrl+h (alt+period also works). Back/Forward/Up are keyboard shortcuts so they reach the focused window (the built-in back/forward click mouse side buttons at the pointer).

profiles.name: Files, Nemo and Thunar
profiles.description: Navigation, new folder, rename, search, hidden files and tabs for GNOME Files, Nemo and Thunar.
profiles.notes: Only keys shared by Nautilus, Nemo and Thunar are used. Not shared, so left out: split view (F3 in Nemo 'Extra Pane' and Thunar, none in Nautilus), open terminal (shift+F4 in Nemo only), reopen closed tab (ctrl+shift+t in Nautilus only; in Nemo it opens the selection in a new tab), copy location (none of them). Close Tab is the built-in ctrl+w. The Nemo/Thunar X11 class names (nemo, thunar) are the conventional lowercase names, not checked on a running window.

profiles.name: Discord
profiles.description: Quick switcher, unread navigation, upload, emoji, mute and deafen for Discord.
profiles.notes: Mark Read (Escape) marks the current channel read; shift+Escape marks the whole server read. Unread Up/Dn jump to the previous/next unread channel. Answer accepts an incoming call (Escape declines). Start call is left out: Discord's help article says ctrl+bracketleft while its blog says ctrl+apostrophe. Discord search (ctrl+f) is not in either source.

profiles.name: Slack
profiles.description: Quick switcher, unreads, upload and huddle controls for Slack.
profiles.notes: Windows/Linux column. Upload is ctrl+o (not ctrl+u). Huddle (ctrl+shift+h) starts, joins or leaves a huddle in the current conversation; Huddle Mic (ctrl+shift+space) toggles mute. Mark Read (Escape) marks the conversation read; shift+Escape marks everything read. Unreads opens All Unreads.

profiles.name: Telegram
profiles.description: Chat and folder navigation, search, saved messages and archive for Telegram Desktop.
profiles.notes: From Telegram's built-in default table (shortcuts.cpp fillDefaults). Mark as read (ctrl+r) is left out because ctrl+r is also bound to Record Voice. Telegram has no default emoji-picker or upload shortcut. ctrl+q quits Telegram and is never used. Saved is Saved Messages (ctrl+0), Top Chat jumps to the first chat (ctrl+alt+Home). WM_CLASS is TelegramDesktop.

profiles.name: Element
profiles.description: Room search, unread navigation, upload and call mic/camera for Element.
profiles.notes: Rooms (ctrl+k) opens room search; Unread Up/Dn jump to the previous/next unread room; 1st Unread jumps to the oldest unread message; Mark Read (Escape) dismisses the read marker. Mic/Camera (ctrl+d/ctrl+e) act in a call. Element has no default emoji picker key and ctrl+f search is off by default. The 'element' X11 class (StartupWMClass=Element) is not verified; im.riot.Riot is the Flathub id.

profiles.name: JetBrains IDEs
profiles.description: Find action, run, debug, navigation, refactoring and VCS for IntelliJ-based IDEs.
profiles.notes: JetBrains picks its default keymap from the desktop (Default for GNOME / Default for KDE / Default for XWin, all based on the Windows/Linux keymap); every key here is identical in all three. Deliberately left out: Reformat Code (ctrl+alt+l in GNOME/XWin but shift+alt+l in the KDE keymap, and ctrl+alt+l locks the screen on Plasma), Stop (ctrl+F2, ctrl+2 on KDE), Navigate Back/Forward (differs on GNOME), and Search Everywhere (double shift, not a chord; Actions ctrl+shift+a is the substitute). Commit (ctrl+k) opens the commit tool window, it does not push. Undo/Redo/Duplicate (ctrl+z, ctrl+shift+z, ctrl+d) are from the reference card. X11 classes follow JetBrains' rule 'jetbrains-' + lowercased product (verified in source); native Wayland app_ids and JetBrains Toolbox desktop file names are not verified.

profiles.name: Kdenlive
profiles.description: Play, cut at playhead, undo, timeline zoom and edit-point navigation for Kdenlive.
profiles.notes: Cut Clip (shift+r) cuts the selected clip at the playhead; Cut All (ctrl+shift+r) cuts every track. Prev/Next Edit are the previous/next snap point (alt+Left/alt+Right). Timeline zoom is ctrl+equal (also ctrl+plus) / ctrl+minus; Fit Zoom to Project has no default key. Redo is ctrl+shift+z (built-in).

profiles.name: Shotcut
profiles.description: Play, split, undo, timeline zoom and edit navigation for Shotcut.
profiles.notes: Linux column of Shotcut's list. Timeline zoom is equal/minus/0 without ctrl (alt+equal/alt+minus zoom the Keyframes panel). Split (s) splits at the playhead; shift+s splits all tracks. Prev/Next Edit are alt+Left/alt+Right (Up/Down change track). Redo accepts ctrl+shift+z (built-in) as well as ctrl+y. DaVinci Resolve is not covered: the only official public shortcut list found is the Resolve 11 macOS PDF, so current Linux defaults could not be verified.

profiles.name: General
profiles.description: Media, volume, screenshot, lock and desktop actions when no app profile matches.
profiles.notes: Modelled on Logitech's default General profile, which Logitech describes only as 'multimedia actions, OS actions, application and file launchers, and an emoji launcher' (no per-key list is published). Volume/Mute/Screenshot use the built-in actions (XF86 volume keys show the desktop's OSD; Screenshot sends Print, which opens the GNOME/KDE Spectacle screenshot UI; sway and Hyprland have no default Print binding). Lock uses loginctl lock-session (needs a locker listening to logind, e.g. hypridle on Hyprland). Calculator launches kcalc, gnome-calculator, qalculate-gtk or xcalc. Transport uses playerctl because there is no built-in previous/next action and it works on every compositor. Files opens the home folder in the default file manager. No emoji key: there is no cross-desktop picker (KDE has plasma-emojier on meta+period; GTK's ctrl+period works only inside GTK text fields). SmartShift and DPI Cycle act on the connected MX mouse.
